text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPLITA
- Around 40 percent of Poles approve of Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and his ways of governing the country while 42 are critical of him, a survey by the PBS polling institute said.
- Poland will not issue bonds to pay for flood damage this year despite the recent demand by the Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) to do so.
A bond issue will be considered for the 1998 public budget, Cimoszewicz said.
- The cabinet has asked the three-party commission of employers, trade unions and the government to consider levying a new tax to cover flood-related losses.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPLITA
- The Milmet SA gas bottle maker, controlled by the National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 2, will list 3,159,750 shares on the Warsaw bourse's parallel market in the first quarter of 1998, Milmet said.
- Poland's pharmaceutical market is underdeveloped compared with other countries in the region.
An average Pole annually consumes pharmaceutics worth $40, a report by ING Barings said.
- The TZMO SA band-aid maker in Torun, northern Poland, received an International Standards Organisation ISO-9001 quality product certificate last week, the company said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- The number of pay cards issued to Polish customers by the country's biggest banks grew by 56 percent in the first half of 1997 compared with the same period last year, a survey by the DPiG business daily showed.
- Ailing Savim Bank Depozytowo Kredytowy is in talks with a potential strategic investor.
National Bank of Poland (NBP) spokeswoman Renata Wisniewska declined to name the prospective investor.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Sales by courier firms operating in Poland reached $80 million in 1996, showing 50-percent growth compared with the year before, but industry analysts are convinced that the real boom in delivery services is still to come.
- The Gdansk Refinery plans to buy the Petrobaltic oil exploration company which operates an off-shore rig in the Baltic sea, the refinery said.
In the first half of 1997 Gdansk Refinery processed 225,000 tonnes of oil from the Baltic deposits.
- Polish construction firms' sales in Germany reached 2 billion marks last year.
In the future the sales will decline significantly due to a recently imposed ban on new construction contracts to be carried out by Polish firms due to EU regulations.
ZYCIE
- The Nike construction material maker plans to invest $3.7 million in road construction material and steel products plant in the Katowice special economic zone in southern Poland.
- The general shareholders meeting of the Ciech chemical trader will appoint a new company president on Tuesday.
The two most favoured candidates are Zdzislaw Matkiewicz, the former president, and Henryk Cuga.
PARKIET

- The Soft-tronic software firm will present a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) by the end of September 1997, the firm's president Stanislaw Winiarski said. NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
